facts.fact_text: The applicant intended to organise a demonstration protesting against "the persecution of national radicalism".
The demonstration was planned to take place between 4 p.m. and 7 p.m. on 15 August 2009.
The planned venue for the demonstration was Venyige Street in Budapest Xth District, in front of Budapest Penitentiary.
On 14 August 2009, Budapest Police Department banned the demonstration.
Because of the prohibition by Budapest Police Department, the demonstration did not take place.
Budapest Police Department banned the demonstration in pursuit of its prerogatives under section 8(1) of Act no. III of 1989 on the Right of Assembly.
Budapest Police Department was of the view that there was no alternative route for traffic in the neighbourhood of Venyige Street.
Budapest Police Department concluded that the demonstration would impede traffic inordinately because there was no alternative route for traffic in the neighbourhood.
According to the Government's submissions, Venyige Street is five metres wide.
According to the applicant's submissions, Venyige Street is eight metres wide.
Parallel to the main driveway of Venyige Street, there is a service lane with a width equivalent to that of two cars.
The service lane parallel to the main driveway of Venyige Street is normally used as a car park.
According to the applicant's submissions, the service lane could have accommodated largely all the demonstration participants without them creating any major traffic incident.
In the notification to Budapest Police Department, the applicant indicated that a maximum of 200 participants were to be expected at the demonstration.
Budapest Police Department was of the view that there was no alternative route for traffic in the neighbourhood of Venyige Street.
Budapest Police Department concluded that the demonstration would impede traffic inordinately because there was no alternative route for traffic in the neighbourhood.
The Budapest Regional Court found that the only valid reason for banning the demonstration was the disproportionate difficulties which would be caused to traffic by the demonstration.
The Budapest Regional Court relied on an expert opinion provided by the Traffic Division of Budapest Police Department.

According to the Traffic Division of Budapest Police Department's expert opinion, the demonstration would have significantly impeded traffic heading to the shops located in Venyige Street, a dead end.

According to the Traffic Division of Budapest Police Department's expert opinion, the demonstration would have significantly impeded traffic heading to the local waste disposal site accessible via Venyige Street.

According to the Traffic Division of Budapest Police Department's expert opinion, the demonstration would have significantly impeded traffic heading to the suppliers' entrance of Budapest Prison via Venyige Street.

According to the Traffic Division of Budapest Police Department's expert opinion, the disruption caused by the crowd might have extended to Maglódi Road, a major thoroughfare in the vicinity of Venyige Street.
